name: Amsterdam municipal giro deposit bank
description: The municipality established a bank intended to accept coin deposits and transfer balances between customers’ accounts by book entry.

impact.note: One city bank modelled on Venice; merchants across Europe settled bills more safely in its book money, and public and central banking drew on it.

date.basis: The historical study dates the municipality’s founding of the bank to 1609.

events.statement: Amsterdam established a publicly owned giro bank.
events.scope: Founding and stated design of one municipal institution.

evidence.supports: Amsterdam established a publicly owned giro bank.
The charter envisaged deposits, account transfers and withdrawals.

contributions.resource: Founded and owned the public payments bank.

evidence.supports: The study attributes founding and ownership to the municipality.

earliest_record.rationale: Date and scope follow the cited event; this is the earliest episode established in this research, not a claim of world priority.

caveats: The charter’s stated functions do not alone establish exactly when each became routine. The bank was modelled on earlier Italian public deposit banks; this record is not a claim of a world first.

research.note: Independent second reader checked the cited historical episodes, dates and actor roles against the stated source passages, subject to the caveats; other facets are not blanket reviewed.
